name: Streaming Context Engineering A Principal Agent Theory Of Ai Augmented Knowledge Work 178C754D12
text: Context Engineering: A Principal-Agent Theory of AI-Augmented Knowledge Work identifies costly, imperfectly observable, expertise-dependent context work as a mechanism creating moral hazard and screening problems inside firms. This extends Kaal's costly-monitoring account from ownership-control conflicts to human effort in AI-augmented knowledge work. The abstract does not establish that the same friction persists between artificial agents operating on fully attested substrates.
